scenario: Agent1 has spent the entire day meticulously cleaning their shared apartment in anticipation of a visit from Agent2's family. Agent2, who had been busy with other commitments, returns to find the apartment spotless. Agent1 expects some form of appreciation or help in maintaining the cleanliness, while Agent2 feels they should not be burdened with extra chores since they did not contribute to the mess. The two must navigate this situation while preparing for the family visit.
learner_goal: Seek acknowledgment for the effort put into cleaning and establish a mutual understanding for maintaining the apartment's cleanliness (<extra_info>Extra information: Agent1 believes that maintaining a clean living space is a shared responsibility and hopes for Agent2's cooperation.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Micah, I spent the whole day cleaning for your family's visit — I was hoping you'd notice. It would mean a lot to get a thanks, and I really want us to share keeping the place tidy; can we agree on a simple plan (like alternating quick tidies or splitting chores) so it doesn't always fall on one of us?

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Giselle, thank you — the place looks amazing and I really appreciate you doing that. You're right: I didn't help today and I should've, so I'm sorry; I don't want upkeep to fall only on you. Can we try a simple plan: alternate a 10-minute evening tidy and split bigger tasks by area (I take kitchen/trash, you take living room/laundry) and rotate weekly or before visits? Does that sound fair?
